prompts.text: What's the most memorable way someone has described their hometown to you?
Tell me about a local custom that surprised you when you first experienced it.
Swap favourite childhood sayings or compare the foods people associate with home?
We both grew up with different words for the same everyday object. Which would you try to teach me first?
A familiar place often sounds new when somebody else describes what they notice.
Asking about someone's hometown is more interesting when you go beyond famous landmarks.
What's a tiny detail about your neighbourhood that makes you smile?
Recall someone showing you a side of their city that tourists rarely see.
A newcomer asks for the most unusual local tradition worth experiencing. What would you recommend?
Take a guided walk through a new neighbourhood or ask a resident for their favourite stories?
What's a word your friends use that a stranger would need explained?
Describe a time you confidently misunderstood an expression someone used.
Learn a funny saying from another language or teach one from your own?
A new acquaintance asks for a friendly phrase they can use in your language. Which would you teach?
People often learn the personality of a language through its everyday jokes.
Good humour travels better when someone explains the context rather than repeating the punchline.
Which expression would you find difficult to translate for somebody new?
Tell me about a word you learnt through a conversation instead of a dictionary.
We create a two-word phrase to describe our first meeting. What should it mean?
Try a tongue-twister from your language or exchange two unusual local proverbs?
Which small decision makes you trust someone's judgement in an unfamiliar place?
Recall a new acquaintance helping you figure out something that seemed confusing.
Ask someone how they solve everyday problems or how they choose what to learn?
A simple task turns into a puzzle while we're together. Would you investigate first or brainstorm out loud?
People show different problem-solving styles even when facing the same tiny inconvenience.
An ability to admit uncertainty makes somebody easier to collaborate with.
What's a skill you admire most when you see somebody demonstrate it casually?
Tell me about watching someone solve a problem in a way you'd never considered.
You're given an unfamiliar piece of equipment and one helpful new acquaintance. How would you divide the task?
Work through a short puzzle together or ask each other to explain one useful life trick?
What's something people assume is everyone's favourite activity but isn't yours?
Describe a time you politely skipped an activity and found a different way to join in.
Try a social game for ten minutes or take a break to chat with another newcomer?
We join a group activity and realise neither of us understands the rules. Who asks for help first?
People often feel more comfortable joining in after someone explains what participation involves.
It's easier to enjoy meeting someone when nobody insists they join every activity.
How do you prefer people invite you to something unfamiliar?
Recall enjoying an event more once you knew you were free to leave early.
A new acquaintance suggests a sport you've never played. What would make you willing to try?
Join a friendly beginner competition or cheer from the sidelines and ask questions?
What's an unusual item you'd pack for a short trip purely because it makes you happy?
Tell me about a travel habit you learnt from somebody you met along the way.
Travel with somebody who takes photographs of everything or one who collects local stories?
We're waiting at an airport and each get to choose a conversation topic with zero travel complaints. What's yours?
Two travellers can visit the same place and return with completely different memories.
A person's curiosity matters more to a trip than how many destinations they tick off.
What's the most interesting thing a fellow passenger has taught you?
Recall learning something about another person's background during a long journey.
A new acquaintance asks you to recommend a journey worth taking even without a final destination. What route comes to mind?
Compare our most surprising travel discoveries or our funniest packing mistakes?
What does someone have to say for you to suspect they're a fellow book lover?
Tell me about a conversation that convinced you to read a book you would otherwise have ignored.
Swap one paragraph from a favourite book or explain a story you wish more people knew?
A new acquaintance challenges you to recommend one story without revealing the genre. What would you say?
People sometimes reveal more about their values through a favourite character than a direct question.
Disagreeing with a story's ending often makes for a better discussion than agreeing about everything.
What kind of character immediately catches your attention in a story?
Recall a book or article that changed the way you viewed a familiar situation.
We pick books for each other based on a ten-minute conversation. What clues would help you choose mine?
Discuss a surprising plot twist or compare the characters we rooted for?
What's a childhood curiosity you still haven't found a satisfying answer to?
Tell me about asking somebody a question and receiving a fascinating unexpected story.
Learn why a familiar tradition began or how an ordinary household invention works?
We're asked to create a tiny exhibition about one everyday curiosity. What would you put in it?
The questions people ask often reveal interests they haven't named as hobbies.
It's worthwhile to ask simple questions even when everyone else seems to know the answer.
What's one topic you enjoy hearing someone explain enthusiastically?
Describe someone who made an unfamiliar subject understandable through a funny comparison.
A new acquaintance is passionate about a subject you know nothing about. What's the first detail you'd ask them to explain?
Listen to a person's unusual hobby story or let them demonstrate a small part of it?
Which harmless superstition did you grow up hearing about?
Tell me about discovering another family's unusual tradition during a visit.
Swap funny childhood warnings or compare the rules adults gave you about good manners?
We each describe a childhood rule without explaining its purpose. Whose rule sounds stranger?
Stories from childhood are often funniest when people realise their homes had different rules.
A childhood myth becomes more entertaining when you learn where the story originated.
What's something your family did that you assumed every household did?
Recall explaining one of your childhood customs to a person who'd never encountered it.
A new friend invites you to a festival you've never attended. What would you want to understand first?
Hear a story about an old celebration or learn how its modern version developed?
What kind of message makes it easy to continue a conversation the next day?
Tell me about somebody who remembered to follow up on a small story you mentioned.
Receive a photo connected to yesterday's conversation or a short question about how things went?
We've been talking for a while and both need to return to work. What's a natural way to leave the conversation open?
Some friendships begin with occasional exchanges rather than constant conversation.
A clear, low-pressure invitation is better than trying to hint at a future meeting.
What helps you tell whether you both want to keep getting to know each other?
Recall an introduction that grew into friendship through a series of brief encounters.
You want to invite someone you recently met to a group event. What information would make the invitation comfortable?
Suggest a specific casual activity or ask a new acquaintance which outings they prefer?
What's one thing you'd be interested to learn about me before choosing another activity together?
Tell me about discovering a surprising shared interest after several conversations.
Share an unusual personal goal or explain one everyday habit you want to improve?
We each get to plan a ten-minute activity that reflects something about us. What would yours be?
The things people enjoy practising often tell you more than their lists of favourites.
Friendship grows more naturally when people leave space for differences in taste.
What's a side of your personality that takes a few conversations to reveal?
Describe someone who made you feel welcome without expecting you to act outgoing.
You meet an acquaintance after a year and both have new interests. How would you get reacquainted?
Explore a shared interest in more depth or introduce each other to something unfamiliar?
